chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, saying: He narrated to me Al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maysami or one of them, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, who mentioned it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to have blood-letting done on Monday after the afternoon prayer.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do on Mondays after the afternoon prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this narration establishes the Sunnah of cupping (hijamah) on Mondays after the afternoon prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating physical well-being with spiritual discipline. It underscores the Prophet’s holistic approach to health, where medicinal practices were synchronized with the rhythm of daily worship, a tradition further validated by later Shia jurists as a recommended act (mustahabb).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-65 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Hussein al-Lu’lu’ee, on the authority of either or both Muhammad ibn Isma’il and Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Maysami, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Mihzam that someone had narrated that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “God’s Prophet (MGB) had blood-letting done on Monday afternoons.”
